name: cloud-libs
description: Ships every constellation library module as its own installable APK.
_doc: ea_cloud-keyboard-libs bundles five modules into ONE companion APK. This repo is the general case: one APK per library module, so each lib is installable, updatable and inspectable on its own. Nothing here names a module - the set comes from scanning lib_apks.scan, so a new module in ea_cloud-superapp/libs/ ships an APK with no edit to this file (FIRE RULE #6).

lib_apks._doc_scan: Every directory under ANY of these paths that contains a build.gradle is a library module and gets an APK. A list because library modules live beside the app that grew them: superapp holds most, while cal/contacts/maps/news/wallet stayed in their own repos. Module names must be unique ACROSS roots - the name is both the gradle path and the applicationId suffix - and settings.gradle fails the build if two roots collide. Paths are relative to this repo's root.
lib_apks._doc_exclude: Modules that must NOT ship as a standalone APK, each with the reason. An exclusion is a claim about install-time behaviour, so it belongs in data next to the scan rule rather than as a silent skip in gradle.

exclude.keyboard: Already ships as its own APK (Cloud-Keyboard.apk, ea_cloud-keyboard). A second package carrying the same LatinIME service would register a duplicate input method, and its clipboard/gesture ContentProvider authorities come from string resources that both packages would claim - INSTALL_FAILED_CONFLICTING_PROVIDER.

lib_apks._doc_ids: Flavor applicationId = <application_id_prefix>.<module name with '-' stripped>; release asset = <asset_prefix><Module-Name>.apk. Derived, never listed.

android._doc_abi_filters: Mirrors ea_cloud-keyboard-libs. Only voice-vosk/translate-mlkit carry .so payloads; the rest are unaffected by this filter. Add 'x86_64' for Waydroid/emulator and rebuild - no gradle edits needed.
android._doc_packaging_excludes: Duplicate files that must not reach the APK. This repo packages 29 unrelated dependency sets through ONE wrapper module, so license/notice collisions are the normal case rather than an exception: libs:wallet pulls com.sun.mail:android-mail AND android-activation, which both carry META-INF/NOTICE.md, and mergeWalletDebugJavaResource failed the WHOLE build - one flavor taking all 29 APKs down with it. ea_cloud-wallet has carried the same block for its own APK all along. Data, not gradle, so the next collision is a one-line edit here. Never add *.kotlin_module: dropping those breaks Kotlin reflection at runtime, silently.

modules._doc: Only the wrapper lives here. The :libs:* modules are appended by settings.gradle from the lib_apks scan above, each pointing at the one canonical directory in ea_cloud-superapp/libs/.

signing._doc: ONE shared Cloud-constellation signing key for ALL Android apps. build.sh::_resolve_signing resolves $VAULT_DIR + sops-decrypts the passwords. NO fallback.

release._doc_kind: 'lib' = a companion APK that ships engines/behaviour rather than UI. data/regen.sh files these under the SuperApp Constellation page's Libs tab instead of Apps. This repo produces MANY of them, so regen.sh expands lib_apks into one fleet entry per module.
release._doc_auto_update: libs:updater is itself one of the shipped modules and reads release.auto_update from the CONSUMING repo. Disabled here on purpose: each library APK has its own GHCR image, while the updater carries a single image name, so a self-update would pull the wrong artifact. Library APKs are updated by the SuperApp's Constellation page (Libs tab), which knows each one's asset.

auto_update._doc_max_installs_per_pass: Most install sessions ONE unattended background pass may open. A background pass cannot show the system install dialog (Android 10+ blocks background activity starts), so each install it starts leaves a tap-to-install notification holding a PackageInstaller session until the user answers it. Unbounded, one pass over the 40-entry fleet opens 40 and the installer hits Android's 50-session cap - 'Too many active sessions for UID'. The remainder is picked up by the next pass. User-initiated 'Update all' is NOT capped: it runs in the foreground where the dialog appears and sessions resolve at once.

ghcr._doc_image: Per-module image name is '<image_prefix><module>' - that is what build.sh pushes. `image` is the repo-level fallback that libs:updater's BuildConfig reads; it is never pushed to, because a library APK does not self-update (see auto_update below).
